components.title: Theia Cloud
components.description: The Theia Cloud operator, service, conversion webhook and landing page that start each person their workspace.

control-implementations.description: What the Theia Cloud releases, rendered offline with the CI site file, and the site's signed evidence export show.

implemented-requirements.description: Every Theia Cloud workload runs one of our rebuilt images by digest.

statements.description: The four Theia Cloud workloads (operator, service, landing page and conversion webhook) each run one container whose image is the image lock's entry for our rebuild of that part, by digest, pulled IfNotPresent; the operator starts session sidecars from our oauth2-proxy image by digest.
statements.remarks: Your organization imports the images from the signed offline bundle into the site registry.

implemented-requirements.description: Theia Cloud runs with the site's session settings.

statements.description: The operator runs one session per person with no eager start, on the site's storage class and requested size, and a site file without a requested size stops the render; the start page keeps persistent storage on and starts the workbench app definition; the app definition has no prewarm pool and takes the site's capacity and idle values. Every Theia Cloud workload runs as non-root with the RuntimeDefault seccomp profile, no privilege escalation and every capability dropped.
statements.remarks: Your organization sets each site's capacity, idle timeout and workspace size in the site file.

implemented-requirements.description: Theia Cloud verifies TLS with the site chain.

statements.description: Every Theia Cloud Ingress is served by HAProxy over TLS with a certificate from site-pki. The Theia Cloud service and operator both mount ConfigMap sterling-site-ca; the operator's Java runtime trusts only its truststore, and its build removes the upstream session probe's trust-all code, refusing an upstream source it does not recognise; the service starts only with a readable site CA and an HTTPS Keycloak address, and its sign-in client requires TLS verification with that CA. No rendered Theia Cloud release turns verification off.
statements.remarks: Your organization operates the site PKI whose chain these services trust.

implemented-requirements.description: The chart's session sidecar defaults are replaced.

statements.description: The Theia Cloud chart's oauth2-proxy defaults are replaced by the site's: the rendered sidecar configuration keeps TLS verification on, sets the session cookie Secure, reads its secrets from mounted files, and none of the chart's public sample secrets is rendered.
statements.remarks: Your organization's install writes the site's own secrets.

implemented-requirements.description: Changes to sessions and workspaces are audited.

statements.description: The cluster audit policy records every create, update, patch and delete of Theia Cloud sessions, workspaces and app definitions at Request level. On the running site, the signed evidence export reports whether the live audit policy covers Session and Workspace records and counts audit events in the last day.
statements.remarks: Your organization reviews the cluster audit records.

implemented-requirements.description: The site verifies the images it runs.

statements.description: On the running site, the signed evidence export counts the images in the site's image lock list and those whose cosign signature, SBOM attestation and provenance attestation verified; the deployment collector passes each only when every locked image, the Theia Cloud images among them, verified.
statements.remarks: Your organization produces the site's evidence export at least weekly with the organization's public signing key.
